summary:
Read-only inventory of the desktop launcher (D:\GitHub\Eglantine, feat/emuden, d7cb68c840), taken from UI strings and headers in src/yuzu/game, src/yuzu/emuden, src/yuzu/configuration/console_*, src/yuzu/util, main_window.cpp, docs/emuden-library.md, docs/emuden-plugins.md and docs/emuden-android.md. Nothing was run or changed; features are listed as the code and docs describe them, not as tested behaviour.

The launcher is about 40k lines of Qt widgets (largest: core_player.cpp 7.1k, game_home.cpp 2.5k, home_library.cpp 2.3k, plugin_screen.cpp 1.3k) on top of the std-only src/emuden library. It splits into: the home screen (rail, shelves, three layouts, search, details page with about 25 actions, collections, smart collections, series, statistics, wishlist, manuals, imports, report); a four-step setup; Settings (Display, Audio, General, Consoles, Library, Online, Family, System, More); the plugin screens (Consoles, console page, Browse, Plugin sources, per-game page); Switch 2 add-ons; system screens (backup, storage, updates, gallery, diagnostics, notifications, child mode, play time, upkeep); online (Drive, RetroAchievements, RomM); PC stores and Steam (scan, tweak tools, shortcuts, remote play); and SteamOS power profiles and sleep.

Main gaps for the rebuild: the Android app re-implements the screens in Kotlin and lacks version grouping, multi-disc controls, plugin source management and the manifest settings editor; the desktop still falls back to emulator dialogs (More menu, Advanced settings, button mapping, firmware and keys, file pickers); PDF manuals open outside the app; persistent state is spread over about a dozen ini/json/txt files keyed by path; the Controllers screen and Switch 2 rows bind directly to emulator settings; Android has second-screen and interface-size features the desktop lacks. The `features` list has one line per feature with its location; `lessons` has ten points for the from-scratch build.

lessons: Build every screen once on one UI layer shared by Windows, Linux and Android. Today the desktop is Qt widgets and Android is a Kotlin copy that already lags (no version grouping, plugin sources, manifest settings editor), which is exactly the drift the owner wants gone.

Keep one persistent store with stable, content- or id-based game keys. State is now spread over shelves.ini, library.ini, shelves-pc.ini, playtime.ini, stats.ini, player.ini, power.ini, startup.ini, netplay.ini, notifications.json and verify.txt, keyed by device paths, which forced Adopt/migration code and blocks sync between devices.
Mark each record as syncable or device-local in the data model itself (PC games, power, tweaks, paths), so the Drive rule is enforced by one admission point instead of parallel files and leak fixes.

Define the engine contract before any screen: launch, surface handover, input, pause overlay, exit, settings schema, add-ons, save locations, play time. The Switch 2 page, Controllers page, add-on switches and firmware state currently reach straight into the emulator's Settings::values and HID types.

Describe settings pages as data (section, row, kind, value source, explanation) rendered by one component. console_menu and console_list_page already point that way, but each screen hand-builds rows and restores selection itself.

No fallbacks to host dialogs: the More menu, Advanced settings, button mapping, firmware/keys install, path pickers, the update dialog and PDF manuals all leave the console interface today. Each needs a native, pad-driven screen or an explicit decision to drop it.

Give the app its own input model: pad family detection, label mapping, glyphs, per-pad tuning and navigation events in one module, independent of any engine. Today detection lives in the emulator's input subsystem and navigation is emulated as keyboard keys.

Run all scanning, metadata, hashing, artwork and network work on a job system with progress and cancellation that posts to the notification centre; the home model should read a cached index at start instead of rescanning. Several changes still need an app restart (language on home, restored shelves).

Treat capabilities as queries (has Steam, has gamescope power daemon, has second display, can start processes, has file-manager access) so one implementation shows or hides features per device instead of per-platform code paths.

Split by feature with small files and tests from the start: core_player.cpp is 7.1k lines and game_home.cpp 2.5k. Keep translations in a format independent of the UI toolkit and make theme, text size, reduced motion and accessibility properties of the shared components rather than per-screen painting.

summary:
Inventory of the libretro ROM player at D:\GitHub\Eglantine (feat/emuden, d7cb68c840), read-only. The engine is src/emuden/corehost (std-only: LibretroCore, CoreSession, rewind, run-ahead, shader chain, netplay lockstep, relay hub, enhancements, texture packs, dual screen, frame pacing). The desktop player is src/yuzu/emuden/core_player.cpp (7,115 lines, one QWidget class with about 90 atomics and 6 mutexes) plus player_* helpers; Android has a second, thinner player (JNI + Kotlin, GLSurfaceView render thread, AAudio) with fewer features (docs/emuden-android.md).

Pause menu: 12 pages (Main, Save slots, Load slots, Options, Cheats, Controls, Sound, Players, Buttons, Discs, Picture settings, Graphics) and about 60 row kinds; a reduced main page for netplay. Overlays: toast, perf HUD, achievement cards, rewind strip, speedrun splits, record mark, crosshairs, waiting/held-still lines, border.

Settings resolve game > console > global defaults > built-in (player.ini), with "Apply to" per page; motion is always per game.

Gating: hardcore (only once a game is known to have a set) removes load state, undo load, rewind, cheats, slow motion, frame step, turbo, macros; netplay removes pause, states, rewind, fast-forward, slow motion, run-ahead, cheats, options, achievements, patches, touch/pointing, motion, Players page; GPU cores lose rewind, run-ahead, clip, recording, netplay.

Performance design: one emulation jthread owns core, audio (SDL stream with drift control), pacing; UI thread owns QOpenGLWidget and shader chain; GPU cores get a shared context with a three-texture swap; four pacing modes with measured fallbacks. Slow/fragile findings: rewind serialises a full state every 2 frames with XOR/RLE (28 ms on DS in unoptimised Android builds); state size probes that serialise; one core per process; GL-only hardware rendering with compatibility profile for legacy GLSL presets; display-sync detection by counting swaps; option-name heuristics per core; PSP lifecycle crash on Android; texture packs by symlink; AVI/MJPEG writer; and two diverging player implementations.

features.feature: PlanPacing: Display, Game, Variable, BlackFrames modes; fallbacks NoDisplayRate, NoMultiple, DisplayTooSlow, NotSynced; max 3% speed skew; BFI needs >=119 Hz
Two-player deterministic lockstep with input delay 2-6, own protocol v1: Hello/Ping/Pong/Start/Input/Hash/State/Delay/Leave, length-prefixed encoder/decoder, no sockets
Hello compatibility check: protocol, core name, core version, game hash+size (cue/m3u files included), BIOS hash; guest takes host options
Desync detection: guest hashes state every 60 frames (FNV-1a over state or system RAM), host sends state, guest replays kept inputs (256 frames); repeated resyncs (5 within 3 s each) end the game
features.notes: Hashing a full state every second is another serialise cost

features.feature: Delay from ping (DelayForPing), either side may change it live; catch-up at 2x when remote is ahead
Stranger limits: 5 s and 256 KiB before a fitting hello, up to four pending connections, 96 MiB message cap, bounds on impossible frames and queued bytes

Room-code relay: text handshake EMUDEN-RELAY 1 HOST/JOIN <6-char code>, replies WAITING/PAIRED/TAKEN/NOROOM/FULL/BAD, socket-free Hub, 1024 rooms, 30 min room wait, 60 s silence limit; standalone emuden-relay daemon (port 55436)

lessons: Write the player once as a portable core (session thread, command queue, settings, menu model, overlays as data) with thin platform shells; today desktop (Qt, 7,115-line CorePlayer) and Android (JNI/Kotlin) are two implementations with very different feature sets.

Define the pause menu as a declarative page/row model with gating predicates (hardcore, netplay, GPU core, capability flags) evaluated in one place, instead of about 60 row ids handled across RefreshMenu, MenuAdjust and MenuActivate switches with gating repeated at ten or more sites.

Replace the ~90 loose atomics and 6 mutexes with one snapshot struct published emulation->UI and one typed command queue UI->emulation; make start asynchronous rather than blocking the UI thread on a promise while pumping UI jobs.

Own the swap chain: render on a dedicated thread to a native surface (EGL/Vulkan-capable abstraction) so pacing uses real present timing; do not infer vsync by counting QOpenGLWidget swaps, redrawing every refresh, and spin-waiting with yield.

Make rewind cheap by design: capture off the emulation thread or less often with adaptive interval, use a SIMD/block delta, avoid cores' state-size probes that serialise, and budget per device; the 2-frame full serialise plus XOR/RLE scan cost up to 28 ms per DS frame on Android before optimisation flags.

Run cores out of process (or at least behind a process-capable interface): libretro allows one core per process, GPU cores crash (PPSSPP lifecycle), and the same boundary can serve the Switch 2 engine contract (launch, surface handover, input, overlay, exit).

Move per-core knowledge (resolution/widescreen/texture-pack option keys, DS layout option, texture folder rules, forced options, BIOS sets, GPU-drawing flag) out of C++ tables and name heuristics into the plugin manifest so new cores need no app release.

Use one audio path with one drift controller on every platform (lock-free ring + callback), and upload frames without a CPU XRGB->RGBA pass or a cross-thread copy; convert legacy GLSL presets so a core/GLES profile suffices and a Vulkan/hardware-context path stays possible.

Cut every dependency on the emulator's frontend: pads come through hid_core EmulatedController, Controllers dialog, PerfHud, Nx2Debug server, Common::PadStyle and <EdenDir> paths; the new app needs its own pad layer (label mapping, glyph families, rumble, motion), HUD and debug transport.

Make netplay and capture portable and standard: sockets and relay client without Qt, interop tested between desktop and Android, a default relay or NAT traversal, and a real encoder/muxer (platform codec) instead of a hand-written MJPEG AVI and APNG that exclude GPU cores.

summary:
All paths are relative to D:\GitHub\Eglantine (branch feat/emuden, HEAD d7cb68c840; codex/android points at the same commit, so the Android work is fully merged).

(a) Android today is two apps in one APK. The inherited Kotlin emulator frontend (package org.yuzu.yuzu_emu, ~200 files, View/Fragment based, libyuzu-android.so) still owns everything for Switch 2: EmulationActivity, touch overlay, quick settings drawer, stats overlay, driver manager, setup, per-game settings. The EmuDEN layer is 23 Kotlin files (about 8k lines, UI built programmatically in two very large Activities) plus about 2.7k lines of JNI over the shared src/emuden library (libemuden-android.so): library, plugin registry, core installer, libretro player on GLES3 + AAudio, second display, online services, netplay. Tests are instrumentation runners plus app_process/JNI harnesses on one Retroid device; no JVM unit tests, no Switch 2 run, no x86_64 runtime, no release/R8 build.

(b) On desktop the Switch 2 emulator is not behind any boundary: MainWindow::BootGame drives Core::System, EmuThread, settings globals, PatchManager and HIDCore directly, and 24 EmuDEN screen files include emulator headers. The quick menu and performance HUD are separate top-level windows floated over the render window and read emulator globals (present-time ring, Settings::values, HIDCore pad state). The only written sketch of a contract is stage 3 of docs/emuden-plugins.md (a C ABI modelled on the Android JNI surface); the only existing out-of-process launcher is ExternalEngine (child process, job object, no surface/overlay/input contract).

An out-of-app engine needs from the app: content path + program index, data/save/firmware/keys/add-on roots, resolved settings (global, console, game) by label, add-on enable list and order, a parent surface or permission to own a window, input ownership rules, user/locale, log/debug endpoints. The app needs back: lifecycle events (loading stages with counts, running, paused, stopped with status/error), title metadata, perf samples, screenshots, applet requests, settings schema, add-on listing/build id, save paths and play time.

lessons: Put the engine boundary in from day one: today BootGame, quick menu, HUD, settings rows and 24 EmuDEN screen files call Core::System, Settings::values, HIDCore and PatchManager directly, which is why the Switch 2 emulator could never be separated. The new app should only ever speak a versioned message contract (launch, lifecycle events, settings by label, perf samples, add-on listing, applet requests) to any engine.

One UI implementation, not two: Android re-implemented the home, details, settings, pause menu, theme and footer in Kotlin Views (EmudenActivity.kt 1682 lines, RetroActivity.kt 1476 lines) by copying the Qt screens; every feature since has existed twice or only on desktop (versions grouping, plugin browse, gallery, splits, cheats). Screens, theme object and focus/navigation model must be one code base with thin platform shells.

The launcher needs its own input layer. Desktop menu navigation and the retro player read pads through the emulator's HIDCore/input_common; Android uses raw KeyEvent/MotionEvent with no label mapping or glyph families. Build one pad abstraction (label mapping, family glyphs, touch, keyboard/mouse, last-input-method tracking) that the UI and the libretro host share, and hand devices to engines explicitly.

Design overlays for surfaces the app does not own. The quick menu and HUD are extra top-level windows polled into place every 100 ms over the render window, with a different drawer on Android. With an out-of-process engine decide per platform up front: engine-owned window with app overlay window (gamescope/Wayland constraints), or engine renders into an app-provided surface; and define the menu chord, button swallowing and pause semantics in the contract.

Platform services behind small interfaces from the start: storage (SAF vs POSIX; cores need real paths, hence MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE), secrets (Keystore vs secret-tool), HTTP/TLS, audio (AAudio vs desktop), displays, process/Intent launch. Android had to retrofit these through JNI callbacks and #ifdefs in shared code; core download logic and netplay session glue (776 lines) ended up duplicated per platform.

One store for per-game records and identity. There are three play-time stores (emulator PlayTimeManager file, desktop player records, Android preferences) and two save-identity schemes (path-based on desktop, content-based on Android), so nothing syncs across devices. Define entry id, content identity, play time, last played, favourites and settings layering once, in the shared core, driven by engine session start/stop events.

Settings must be schema-driven end to end. Switch 2 settings exist as about 60 legacy Qt dialogs, a console menu bound to Settings::BasicSetting pointers, manifest rows with illustrative native_setting labels, and a separate Android settings tree. Have each engine publish its schema (key, type, range, scope, runtime-modifiable) and generate Settings / Consoles / per-game pages from it on every platform.

Keep the build small and separable: the Android app builds the whole emulator tree through the root CMakeLists, needs a host glslangValidator, pins NDK r29 because of Dynarmic, and ships a 117 MB APK; the launcher library already proved it can build alone (tools/native-check). The new repo should build the app without any engine present and treat 'engine not installed' as a normal state.

Test on every target from one harness and cover what was skipped. Current evidence is one arm64 device with custom instrumentation using reflection on private fields; Switch 2 launch, x86_64 runtime, release/R8, backup, real accounts, audio and human pad input were never verified, and host online tests cannot link. Give the app a built-in automation endpoint (status, screenshot, input injection) like the emulator's debug server, usable on Windows, SteamOS and Android in CI.

Decide Android engine delivery and store constraints before writing the contract: a Surface cannot simply be handed to another process, downloaded native code and MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE both conflict with Play policy, Vulkan is marked required in the manifest, and Drive sync depends on Play services with per-certificate OAuth clients. The Switch 2 engine on Android is realistically a separately installed package or sideloaded signed library, and the contract (Intent/binder vs C ABI) should be chosen for that, not assumed identical to the PC child-process model.
